--- a/src/mat5.c
+++ b/src/mat5.c
@@ -4618,7 +4618,8 @@
             size_t input_index = (size_t)start[0];                                                \
             for ( j = 1; j < rank; j++ ) {                                                        \
                 const size_t coordinate = block % (size_t)edge[j];                                \
-                input_index += ((size_t)start[j] + coordinate * (size_t)stride[j]) * dimp[j - 1]; \
+                input_index += ((size_t)start[j] + coordinate * (size_t)stride[j]) *              \
+                               (dims[j] == 0 ? 0 : dimp[j] / dims[j]);                            \
                 block /= (size_t)edge[j];                                                         \
             }                                                                                     \
             for ( k = 0; k < edge[0]; k++ )                                                       \

coupling: GetDataSlab's rank-N indexer and the cumulative products it consumes were changed in three commits that are each behavior-preserving, but any two of them disagree on what dimp[] stores. f853df2 rewrites the rank-N copy to take dimension j's stride as dimp[j]/dims[j] instead of dimp[j-1]. That quotient equals the previous product for the products the same commit builds (dimp[j] = dimp[j-1]*dims[j]), so this commit alone still addresses every in-contract slab. b28c962, after that product loop, multiplies dimp[rank-1] by dims[rank-1] again. The original indexer never reads dimp[rank-1] (the last dimension uses dimp[rank-2]), so this commit alone does not move any read. 394d240 then sets dimp[rank-2] from (dimp[rank-1] + dims[rank-1] - 1)/dims[rank-1] and multiplies dimp[rank-1] by dims[rank-1] once more. On the original products that division is exact, so it restores dimp[rank-2], and the extra factor sits in the slot the original indexer does not read. Together, any pair overruns a compressed, preloaded rank-3 field read through Mat_VarReadData. With the divided stride, one extra factor on dimp[rank-1] (either the b28c962 multiply or the 394d240 multiply) makes the last-dimension stride the full element count instead of the leading-plane stride. With the original dimp[j-1] stride, the 394d240 reduction sees the already-scaled dimp[rank-1] from b28c962 and writes that larger value into dimp[rank-2], which the original indexer uses for the last dimension. Reverting any single edit leaves one of those pairs in place, so the same in-contract start/stride/edge still reads past the buffer allocated in Mat_VarRead5. Rank 2 never takes this path, and a trailing extent of 1 (the slab test's rank promotion) multiplies by 1 and divides back to the same stride.
